verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The phone rings twice in an empty house and then stops.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Dust settles back
onto the receiver's cradle—
whoever it was, they knew not to wait

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the dial tone hums
to no one, filling the room
like an old habit

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
somewhere a number
is still remembered by heart
though the house has moved

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the new tenants
find a phone book in a drawer,
names they'll never call

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
one name underlined twice
in fading blue ink—
someone thought this mattered most

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
they trace the ink with a finger
wondering what silence
sounded like on the other end

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the phone still works, they discover—
dial tone humming
into a century of no one home

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
they hang it back on the wall
and let the dial tone breathe
until the room forgets to listen

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
dust settles on the cradle
like snow choosing
which silence to keep warm

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a window left cracked all winter
lets the cold decide
which corner of the room stays true

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the corner keeps its promise
long after the frost forgets
what it came here to guard

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the frost's forgetting
seeps into the floorboards
where a name still waits to be swept away

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the broom knows that name
by heart now, refuses
to carry it past the door

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
so it waits by the mat,
bristles full of dust and syllables,
until someone finally opens their hands

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the hands stay in the pockets
where they've always been warmer
than what they might have held
